description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of shares for different news sources as reported in a study of narrative media framing in political discourse. The chart contains 15 slices representing individual news outlets or a combined “Other” category. Starting with the largest slice and proceeding clockwise, “Other” is grey and accounts for 14% of the total, followed by Shareblue at 13%, and then The Huffington Post, NPR, Vox, and The Guardian each representing 8%, 7%, 6%, and 5% respectively. The next slices are BBC and RT at 5% and 3% respectively, followed by Daily Kos, National Review, and Daily Mail at 3% each. Fox News and CNN each account for 3%, while PoliticusUSA represents 3%. Finally, there are several smaller slices representing Drudge Report, and several sources each at 3%. The chart includes percentage labels displayed inside each slice, and a legend identifying each news source. The slices appear to be ordered from largest to smallest proportion, moving clockwise around the circle.
